references.text: God reveals himself to Abraham and commands him to walk before his presence, which directly mirrors Jacob's words that the fathers Abraham and Isaac walked before God's presence.
Abraham describes God as the one he has walked before, and who will send his angel – a parallel to Jacob's reference to God as the one his fathers walked before.
God appears to Isaac and confirms the promise given to Abraham, which underscores God's faithfulness through generations from Abraham to Isaac.
God gives Jacob promises in Bethel to preserve him wherever he goes, which is the background for Jacob's confession that God has been his shepherd all his life.
David's psalm 'The Lord is my shepherd' expresses the same image of God as shepherd that Jacob uses when he says 'God who has been my shepherd'.
God is referred to as Israel's shepherd, who leads Joseph like a flock – a direct parallel to Jacob's reference to God as his shepherd in the blessing of Joseph.
Noah walked with God, an expression that parallels Jacob's mention that his fathers Abraham and Isaac walked before God's presence.
The Epistle to the Hebrews specifically notes that Jacob in faith blessed Joseph's two sons, a direct reference to the blessing where Jacob invokes God's shepherdly care.
Both verses confirm God's unbroken faithfulness (hesed) toward the individual throughout life or a journey.
Jacob uses an identical address to the God of his fathers at two crucial moments in his life (deliverance and blessing), which underscores the continuity of his faith.
